English Grade XI · Fase F · Functional Text

Formal Communications

Learn how to write formal letters and professional emails for permission, cooperation, cover letters, and sponsorship proposals. This chapter connects English learning with real communication needs in school, study, work, and island community life.

Text Type Formal Letter & Email
Language Polite requests & Passive Voice
Project Sponsorship Email
Mode Interactive Student Module
Part 1

Chapter Opening: From Chat Messages to Professional Communication

Situational Hook: OSIS, English Club, atau panitia kelas XI ingin mengadakan English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program. Panitia membutuhkan dukungan berupa air minum, alat tulis, hadiah lomba, transportasi lokal, atau dana kegiatan. Mereka tidak bisa hanya menulis “Halo kak, sponsor dong buat kegiatan kami.” Mereka perlu mengirim email resmi yang jelas, sopan, dan profesional.

Dalam kehidupan sehari-hari, kamu mungkin sering menulis pesan singkat kepada teman. Namun, ketika kamu menghubungi kepala sekolah, guru, panitia, sponsor, kampus, perusahaan, instansi, alumni, atau calon mitra kegiatan, kamu perlu menggunakan bahasa yang lebih resmi.

Dalam chapter ini, kamu akan belajar menulis formal letter dan formal email untuk meminta izin resmi, mengajukan kerja sama, menulis cover letter sederhana, menghubungi calon sponsor, menyampaikan proposal kegiatan, dan meminta informasi secara sopan.

Professional Example

English: We would be grateful if your organization could support our English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program by providing student learning materials or other forms of sponsorship.

Arti: Kami akan sangat berterima kasih jika organisasi Bapak/Ibu dapat mendukung kegiatan English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program kami dengan menyediakan perlengkapan belajar siswa atau bentuk sponsorship lainnya.

Part 6

Context Exploration: Why Formal Communication Matters

Why It Matters

Formal communication helps people communicate clearly, politely, and professionally. It is useful for asking permission, contacting a teacher or principal, applying for a program, requesting cooperation, asking for sponsorship, contacting a university, and communicating with external partners.

Island School Context

  • meminta izin karena kapal terlambat
  • mengirim surat izin mengikuti lomba di daratan
  • menghubungi alumni untuk dukungan English Club
  • mengajukan proposal kegiatan literasi pesisir
  • meminta kerja sama dengan komunitas lingkungan
  • mengirim email kepada sponsor lokal
  • meminta informasi beasiswa atau kegiatan kampus
Part 7

Genre Focus: Functional Text — Formal Letter and Formal Email

Functional Text

A functional text is a text used for a practical purpose in daily life.

Formal Letter

A formal letter is a written message used for official or professional purposes.

Formal Email

A formal email is an electronic message written in a professional format and tone.

AspectFormal LetterFormal Email
MediumPrinted or digital documentSent electronically
AddressUsually includes sender and recipient addressesUses email address fields
Subject lineUsually not written as a separate email fieldVery important
SignatureHandwritten or typedTyped name and identity
UseOfficial documents, permissions, applicationsFast professional communication
Social Function: to communicate official or professional messages clearly, politely, and effectively.

Language Focus: Greetings, Polite Requests, and Passive Voice

Formal Greetings and Closings

GreetingUseExample
Dear Sir or Madam,When you do not know the recipient’s nameDear Sir or Madam, I am writing to request sponsorship.
Dear Mr. Hasan,For a male recipient whose name is knownDear Mr. Hasan, we would like to invite you to our event.

Less PoliteMore Polite

Passive Voice for Formal Context

Basic Pattern: be + past participle / V3. Passive voice is used because it sounds more objective and focuses on the action, process, or result.
Active VoicePassive VoiceArti Passive Voice

Part 15

Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Subject Line Is Too General

Weak: Help

Better: Sponsorship Request for English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program

Mistake 2: Greeting Is Too Casual

Weak: Hi kak,

Better: Dear Mr. Hasan,

Mistake 3: Purpose Is Not Clear

Weak: We want to talk about our activity.

Better: We are writing to request sponsorship for our English Camp.

Mistake 4: Request Sounds Too Demanding

Weak: You must give us support.

Better: We would be grateful if your company could support our program.

Mistake 5: No Sender Identity

Weak: We need your help.

Better: My name is Aulia Rahman, a member of the student committee.

Mistake 6: Too Much Chat Language

Weak: Pls help us. Thx.

Better: We would appreciate your support. Thank you for your attention.

Mistake 7: Wrong Passive Voice

Weak: The event will held on Saturday.

Better: The event will be held on Saturday.

Mistake 8: Attachment Is Missing

Weak: The proposal is attached, but no file is attached.

Better: Check the attachment before sending the email.

Part 16–19

Model Texts

Model Text 1: Formal Email — Requesting Permission

To: english.teacher@sman6pangkep.sch.id

Subject: Permission Request to Attend English Speech Competition

Dear Ms. Rahma,

My name is Nur Aisyah, a student of Grade XI at SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan. I am writing to request your permission to attend the English Speech Competition in Makassar on Saturday, 18 October 2026.

The competition will be held at Hasanuddin University from 08.00 a.m. to 03.00 p.m. I have been selected to represent our school in the speech category. The invitation letter has been sent by the organizing committee, and the registration form has been completed.

Since I need to travel from the island to Makassar, I may leave school one day earlier depending on the boat schedule. I will make sure to complete all assignments before leaving and submit any missing work after the competition.

I would be grateful if you could give me permission and guidance before the event. Thank you for your attention and consideration.

Sincerely,
Nur Aisyah
Grade XI Student
SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan

Model Text 2: Formal Email — Cooperation Request

To: coastalcare.community@email.com

Subject: Cooperation Request for Island Youth Environmental Campaign

Dear Coastal Care Community Team,

We are the student committee of SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan. We are writing to propose a collaboration for our upcoming program entitled “Island Youth Environmental Campaign.”

The program will be held on Friday, 24 October 2026, at our school and the nearby coastal area. This activity is designed to improve students’ environmental awareness and English communication skills. During the program, students will create English campaign posters, deliver short speeches, and participate in a coastal clean-up activity.

We kindly request your cooperation as a community partner. Your team’s experience in environmental education would be valuable for our students. We would appreciate it if your team could provide a short sharing session about plastic waste reduction and safe coastal clean-up practices.

The event proposal is attached to this email for your review. We hope this collaboration can create a meaningful learning experience for students and strengthen environmental awareness in our island community.

Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to your response.

Best regards,
Student Committee
SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan

Model Text 3: Simple Cover Letter

Dear Volunteer Program Coordinator,

I am writing to apply for the volunteer position in the Youth Literacy Program. My name is Ahmad Fikri, and I am a Grade XI student at SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan.

I am interested in this opportunity because I enjoy reading, speaking English, and helping younger students learn. I have experience as a member of the English Club, where I participated in storytelling activities and public speaking practice. I also served as a class committee member, so I am familiar with teamwork and responsibility.

I believe my communication skills, motivation, and willingness to learn can support this program. I am available to join the volunteer training and participate in the scheduled activities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to contribute to this program.

Sincerely,
Ahmad Fikri
Grade XI Student
SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan

Model Text 4: Sponsorship Email for School External Activity

To: partnership@nusantarabeverage.co.id

Subject: Sponsorship Request for English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program

Dear Partnership Team of Nusantara Beverage,

My name is Siti Aulia, and I am writing on behalf of the English Club Committee of SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan. We would like to introduce our upcoming student program entitled “English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program.”

The event will be held on Saturday, 15 November 2026, at SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan and the nearby coastal area. This program is designed to improve students’ English communication skills, leadership, teamwork, and environmental awareness. The participants will join public speaking practice, coastal literacy activities, poster presentations, and a plastic waste reduction campaign.

Through this email, we would like to request sponsorship from Nusantara Beverage. We would be grateful if your company could support this program by providing drinking water, student learning kits, prizes, or other forms of contribution. The support will be used to help students participate actively and comfortably during the program.

As a sponsor, your company’s logo will be displayed on the event banner, student certificates, and social media publication. Your support will also be acknowledged during the opening and closing ceremonies.

Please find attached our event proposal for your review. We hope you will consider our sponsorship request positively. Should you need further information, please feel free to contact us at englishclub.sman6@email.com.

Thank you for your time, attention, and consideration. We look forward to your response.

Sincerely,
Siti Aulia
English Club Committee
SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan

Part 20

Reading Section

Reading Text: Request for Support for Student Leadership and Public Speaking Day

To: communityrelations@bintanglaut.co.id

Subject: Support Request for Student Leadership and Public Speaking Day

Dear Community Relations Team,

We are the Student Leadership Committee of SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan. We are writing to request your support for our upcoming program entitled “Student Leadership and Public Speaking Day.”

The program will be held on Saturday, 22 November 2026, at our school hall. This activity is designed to help students develop leadership, confidence, teamwork, and English communication skills. The participants will take part in leadership workshops, public speaking practice, group discussions, and a student presentation session.

As students from an island school, we believe that communication skills are important for our future study, work, and community participation. Many students have great ideas, but they need more opportunities to practice speaking confidently and professionally.

We would be grateful if your company could support this program by providing stationery, student notebooks, drinking water, or prizes for the participants. The support will be used to help students participate actively in all sessions. Your company’s logo will be displayed on the event banner and student certificates.

The event proposal is attached to this email for your review. We hope you will consider our request positively. Should you need further information, please contact us at studentleadership.sman6@email.com.

Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to your response.

Sincerely,
Student Leadership Committee
SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan

🔊 Buka TTS Listening Browser Mode

TTS ini hanya membaca Listening Script.

Status TTS: siap.

📜 Buka Listening Script

Dina: We need to send the sponsorship email today. Have you written the subject line?

Arman: Yes. I wrote, “Please help our event.”

Dina: I think that sounds too informal. From my perspective, the subject line should be more specific.

Arman: What should we write then?

Dina: How about “Sponsorship Request for English Camp and Coastal Literacy Program”?

Arman: That sounds more professional. What about the opening?

Dina: We should introduce ourselves first. For example, “We are the English Club Committee of SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan.”

Arman: Good idea. Then we can explain that the event will be held next month.

Dina: Yes, and we should use polite language. Instead of saying “Give us support,” we can write, “We would be grateful if your company could support our program.”

Arman: Should we mention the proposal?

Dina: Of course. We can write, “The event proposal is attached to this email for your review.”

Arman: Great. Before sending it, we should check the grammar, attachment, and closing.

Dina: Exactly. A professional email should be clear, polite, and complete.

  3. Dina suggests “Sponsorship Request for English Camp and ________ Literacy Program.”
  4. The committee should ________ themselves first.
  5. The event proposal is ________ to the email.
  6. A professional email should be clear, polite, and ________.

True or False

  1. Arman’s first subject line is already formal and specific.
  2. Dina suggests a more specific subject line.
  3. The sender should introduce themselves in the opening.
  4. The phrase “Give us support” is polite and professional.

  6. The email should be checked before it is sent.

Part 23

Speaking Section: Conversation Practice

Conversation 1: Asking How to Start a Formal Email

Nadia: I need to write an email to a sponsor, but I do not know how to start.

Rizal: You should begin with a formal greeting.

Nadia: Can I write “Hi Kak”?

Rizal: Not for a formal email. It is better to write “Dear Sir or Madam.”

Nadia: After the greeting, what should I write?

Rizal: Introduce yourself and state your purpose clearly.

Nadia: So I can write, “My name is Nadia, and I am writing on behalf of the student committee.”

Rizal: Exactly. That sounds professional.

Speaking Practice: Practice the dialogue with a partner. Change the context, recipient, or event name.

Conversation 2: Discussing a Subject Line

Fira: I wrote the subject line: “Important.”

Doni: I think it is too general. The recipient may not understand the topic.

Fira: What should I write?

Doni: You should mention the purpose and the event.

Fira: How about “Sponsorship Request for School Literacy Festival”?

Doni: That is much better. It is clear and specific.

Speaking Practice: Practice the dialogue with a partner. Change the context, recipient, or event name.

Conversation 3: Making a Polite Request to a Sponsor

Aulia: We need support for our English Camp. Can we write, “Give us drinking water and prizes”?

Haris: That sounds too direct. We need to make it more polite.

Aulia: What should we say?

Haris: We can write, “We would be grateful if your company could support our program by providing drinking water or prizes.”

Aulia: That sounds better. It is polite and clear.

Haris: Yes. We should also explain how the support will be used.

Speaking Practice: Practice the dialogue with a partner. Change the context, recipient, or event name.

Conversation 4: Revising Informal Language

Salsa: I wrote, “Hi, we wanna ask for help. Please reply fast.” Is it okay?

Mira: It is understandable, but it is too informal for a sponsor.

Salsa: How can I revise it?

Mira: Change “Hi” to “Dear Sir or Madam.”

Salsa: What about “we wanna ask for help”?

Mira: You can write, “We would like to request your support for our school program.”

Speaking Practice: Practice the dialogue with a partner. Change the context, recipient, or event name.

Conversation 5: Preparing to Send a Proposal Email

Raka: Are we ready to send the sponsorship email?

Intan: Let’s check it first. Does it have a clear subject line?

Raka: Yes. It says, “Sponsorship Request for Island Youth Environmental Campaign.”

Intan: Good. Did we introduce ourselves?

Raka: Yes. We wrote that we are the student committee of SMAN 6 Pangkajene dan Kepulauan.

Intan: Did we mention the attachment?

Raka: Yes. We wrote, “The event proposal is attached to this email for your review.”

Intan: Great. Now check the grammar and make sure the proposal file is attached.

Speaking Practice: Practice the dialogue with a partner. Change the context, recipient, or event name.
Role-Play Task: Choose one situation: asking a teacher how to write a permission email, discussing a sponsorship email, revising informal language, asking a university staff member for scholarship information, or applying for a volunteer program. Use at least one formal greeting, one purpose statement, one polite request, one passive voice sentence, and one formal closing.
Part 24–26

Writing Section

How to Write a Formal Email

Planning

  1. Who is the recipient?
  2. What is your purpose?
  3. What event are you writing about?
  4. What request do you want to make?
  5. What attachment should be included?

Drafting Structure

PartGuiding Question
SubjectWhat is the email about?
GreetingWho are you addressing?
OpeningWho are you?
PurposeWhy are you writing?
DetailsWhat should the recipient know?
Polite RequestWhat do you request politely?
AttachmentWhat document is attached?
ClosingHow do you end respectfully?
Formal Email Template

To: _______________________________

Subject: _______________________________

Dear _______________________________,

My name is _______________________________, and I am writing on behalf of _______________________________.

I am writing to / We are writing to _______________________________.

The event/program/activity will be held on _______________________________ at _______________________________. This activity is designed to _______________________________.

We would be grateful if you could _______________________________.

Please find attached _______________________________ for your review.

Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to your response.

Sincerely,
_______________________________

Student Role

  • chairperson of the student committee
  • secretary of the English Club
  • OSIS representative
  • event coordinator
  • public relations team member

  3. alumni association

  7. local transportation provider
  8. community health center
  9. small business owner
  10. local government office

  5. Plastic-Free School Campaign
  6. English Debate and Public Speaking Competition
  7. Digital Literacy for Island Students
  8. Coastal Reading Day

Clear subject line
Formal greeting
Sender identity
Event title
Event date and place

Sponsorship request
Forms of support requested
Benefits for sponsor

Signature

Enrichment, Remedial, and Chapter Summary

Enrichment Activities

  1. Write a more professional sponsorship email with sponsor benefits.
  2. Create a one-page proposal summary in English.
  3. Write a simple cover letter for a volunteer program.
  4. Prepare a sponsor pitch presentation.
  5. Compare two formal emails and evaluate which is more effective.
  6. Write a follow-up email after sending a proposal.

Remedial Activities

  1. Memorize 10 formal greetings and closings.
  2. Complete a formal email template.
  3. Revise informal sentences into formal sentences.
  4. Practice writing subject lines.
  5. Identify parts of a formal email.
  6. Complete polite request sentences.
  7. Change active sentences into passive voice.

In this chapter, you have learned that formal communication is important for school, study, work, organization, and future opportunities. You learned how to identify formal letters and formal emails, understand email structure, write clear subject lines, use formal greetings and closings, make polite requests, use passive voice, revise informal language, analyze emails and cover letters, write permission emails, cooperation emails, cover letters, sponsorship emails, and prepare a professional email for a school activity sponsor.

Key Message: A professional email should be clear, polite, complete, and purposeful.
